accuracy.evidence: Claims checked against sources: the Cornell layout (notes column, narrower cue column, summary strip) follows Pauk and Owens, How to Study in College; the verbatim-notes finding follows Mueller and Oppenheimer (2014) with the adult text noting that later replications (Morehead, Dunlosky and Rawson 2019; Urry and colleagues 2021) found the laptop effect smaller; rereading and highlighting as low utility follows Dunlosky and colleagues (2013); recall beating rereading after a week, with rereaders more confident, follows Roediger and Karpicke (2006). Word and character limits in the lab are labelled as a guide, not a rule.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the beliefs pupils hold about notes: copying everything is thorough (step 1 word count feedback, step 2 copy option, p1, m1, challenge 'copy'), any rewording is a paraphrase (step 2 meaning-change options for some/all and why bees dance, p3, m7, challenge 'mean'), the shortest note is best (step 3 over-short feedback, m3, challenge 'short'), the cue column is for notes and the summary goes first (step 4 wrong-zone feedback, p5, m2, challenge 'cue' and 'summary'), and rereading or highlighting is good revision (step 5 peeking feedback, m4, m9, visual sorter, challenge 'reread').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagcornell builds one set of notes on bees across the steps: tap to keep key words with a live word count, pick the faithful paraphrase among a copy and a meaning-changing rewrite, tap phrases to swap in shorthand under a character budget with a readability check, drag pieces into a Cornell page, then cover the notes and answer cue questions from memory. flaggist finds main ideas in paragraphs and builds summaries; flaghworg plans homework; neither has paraphrase checking, a shorthand budget, a Cornell page or cover-and-recall. The lab_distinct gate passes under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each idea comes from doing it: the word counter shows the sentence shrinking from 24 words while every key idea stays, the copy option is rejected because it involves no thinking, the shorthand budget fails if key words are reduced to letters, misplaced Cornell pieces bounce back with the reason for each zone, and the cover step only accepts answers made with the notes covered.

predictions.evidence: Three steps ask for a prediction before the learner acts: step 1 asks whether copied sentences or short own-word notes help more a week later, step 3 asks whether the shortest note is always best, and step 5 asks whether reading notes three times or covering them and answering cue questions helps more for a test. Each answer is then tested in the step itself and revisited in the feedback.

challenge_feedback.evidence: The challenge mixes seven question types (copy, no notes, meaning change, over-short shorthand, cue column, summary timing, rereading). Each wrong choice gets a specific reason tied back to the step where it was practised, for example that rereading feels easy and fools you, or that the summary comes last when the whole page is visible.

readability.evidence: Learner text for ages 11 to 12 uses short sentences and one idea per paragraph, with key terms (key words, paraphrase, shorthand, Cornell page, cue column, summary) explained where they first appear. The adult text names curriculum links and the three common mistakes. The validators' readability checks pass.

no_filler.evidence: Every paragraph adds a new step of the method or a reason it works, with concrete bee examples rather than generic study advice. No praise padding, no repeated key idea, and the filler regex and explanation-overlap gates pass.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 and desktop in light and dark themes: word chips wrap into rows with large tap targets, paraphrase options stack as full-width cards that can be tapped or dragged, the Cornell zones resize to the stage width, and all controls fit without sideways scrolling.

accessibility.evidence: Every action works by tap as well as drag, the canvas has an aria-label and live text status, colour is never the only signal (counts and words accompany each state), and the axe checks pass in light and dark themes with zone labels drawn in dark ink on pale fills.
